chapters.title: Cloud Run release experiment and ECS comparison
chapters.body:
## Container release before cloud deployment

First pass the complete local container and isolated-restore experiment in session 31. Use an image registry with immutable revision tags. Never put provider keys in Docker build arguments, image layers or React variables. Supply runtime credentials from the platform's secret manager and use a least-privilege service identity. The voice gateway's static token, SQLite workspace fixture and process-local limits are deliberately local experiments; they are not the production identity, durable multi-replica workflow or shared quota implementation.

## Cloud Run deployment experiment

Prerequisites: an explicitly selected Google Cloud project with billing enabled, permission to deploy, an Artifact Registry repository, an existing managed PostgreSQL database/private connectivity, a configured service account, and Secret Manager entries. These commands can incur costs. Use your own operator-selected names and quotas. No resources are provisioned by this academy.

Save the following as deploy.sh. It refuses missing configuration, builds the supplied production application image, deploys a candidate without unauthenticated access, and bounds instance and request concurrency. `SERVICE_IMAGE_SOURCE` must point to your production HTTP gateway with a dependency-backed `/api/health/` endpoint and a listener on `$PORT`; it is not the unmodified local Compose topology.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
: "${CLOUD_PROJECT:?Set your authorized project}"
: "${CLOUD_REGION:?Set your region}"
: "${IMAGE_REPOSITORY:?Set the existing regional registry repository}"
: "${SERVICE_NAME:?Set a new test service name}"
: "${SERVICE_ACCOUNT:?Set the approved runtime service identity}"
: "${SERVICE_IMAGE_SOURCE:?Set the production image source folder}"
: "${DATABASE_SECRET:?Set an existing database URL secret name}"
: "${REVISION_TAG:?Set an immutable source revision tag}"
IMAGE="$CLOUD_REGION-docker.pkg.dev/$CLOUD_PROJECT/$IMAGE_REPOSITORY/$SERVICE_NAME:$REVISION_TAG"
gcloud builds submit "$SERVICE_IMAGE_SOURCE" --project "$CLOUD_PROJECT" --tag "$IMAGE"
gcloud run deploy "$SERVICE_NAME" --project "$CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$CLOUD_REGION" \
  --image "$IMAGE" --service-account "$SERVICE_ACCOUNT" \
  --no-allow-unauthenticated --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 \
  --concurrency 8 --timeout 300 --cpu 1 --memory 1Gi \
  --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_SECRET:latest"
URL=$(gcloud run services describe "$SERVICE_NAME" --project "$CLOUD_PROJECT" --region "$CLOUD_REGION" --format='value(status.url)')
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token)
curl --fail --max-time 20 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$URL/api/health/"
```

The values above are small test bounds, not throughput claims. IAM protects this operator experiment; a browser-facing SaaS needs its own authenticated access architecture. Configure the image for its database network and the application’s actual configuration names before running. Run migrations once as a release job against the selected schema, not concurrently in every replica. Pin the tested secret version in the release manifest rather than leaving `latest` in a reproducibility claim. Add a startup/readiness check that verifies the required datastore, and keep provider availability distinct from gateway readiness.

WebSockets are long-lived HTTP requests and remain subject to the platform request timeout. The client must reconnect with bounded backoff, reauthenticate and restore only owner-bound checkpoint state; it must not blindly replay audio or uncertain writes. State, quotas and background jobs must survive replacement of any instance. A configured concurrency of eight is not evidence that eight live audio streams meet the latency target.

## Load, rollback and cleanup evidence

Use a separate synthetic tenant and increment offered concurrency through 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 with a fixed request/audio/context distribution. Record admitted/completed/rejected/failed work, queue time, p50/p95, review quality, provider requests/usage and total spend. Stop on a critical isolation failure or your configured spend/latency boundary. Budget alerts are notification, not a hard spending cap; enforce admission and maximum work before provider calls.

Record the previous healthy Cloud Run revision name before promotion. To roll back, use `gcloud run services update-traffic "$SERVICE_NAME" --to-revisions "$PREVIOUS_REVISION=100" --region "$CLOUD_REGION" --project "$CLOUD_PROJECT"` only after setting PREVIOUS_REVISION to the verified prior revision. Re-run readiness, owner denial and readback after rollback. Do not roll back a schema destructively; rehearse backward-compatible migration and isolated restore. Delete only this disposable test service when the experiment is finished; review registry, database and secret resources separately because deleting the service does not remove their ongoing costs.

## ECS comparison and GPU decisions

ECS expresses the same boundaries through a task definition, service desired count/autoscaling, private subnets/security groups, an application load balancer, Secrets Manager runtime injection and a separate migration task. Distinguish the task execution role (pull image/logs) from the application task role. Set container CPU/memory, load-balancer readiness, deregistration/draining and graceful termination. Store durable state outside tasks and use the same dataset/report for a platform comparison; more orchestration is a maintenance cost to measure.

A local or hosted Ollama/vLLM service adds a different capacity bottleneck: GPU memory, KV cache, batching and output length. Keep a separate GPU service from the web admission tier, authenticate its endpoint, restrict network exposure and measure its model/quantization-specific capacity. The five-slot arithmetic exercise is not a hardware benchmark. Promote a hybrid routing rule only after the same held-out tasks show an acceptable quality floor, data-residency compliance and useful-output savings over the fixed baseline.

chapters.title: Apply the three engineering pillars
chapters.body:
## Software-first practice

Build interfaces, asynchronous services, API adapters and recoverable data flows before studying algorithm derivations. Use mathematics to explain a measured engineering decision.

## Production evidence

A notebook or chat demo is an early prototype. Graduation builds toward operational evidence: deployment/readiness, bounded work, rate limits, error recovery and persisted state. Early checkpoints assess only boundaries already taught; future deployment controls are planned rather than claimed complete. The 10% framing is a teaching heuristic, not a measured universal percentage.

## Apply the three pillars to A multi-user AI service deployed from containers

### Latency vs. Cost vs. Quality

Load-test offered vs. completed work, p95 and cost per accepted result at stated concurrency. Autoscaling settings are hypotheses until observed against downstream/GPU limits.

### Deterministic Evaluation

Test readiness against the actual database, restart/readback, isolated restore, denied owner access, overload rejection and a dependency outage on the deployed revision.

### Context Management

Budget resident model memory/KV cache and per-request context separately. Keep tenant/revision-aware application caches; never assume a process-local cache is shared across replicas.

## Failure and deployment work

Separate request concurrency, worker capacity and model/GPU capacity. Add admission control, shared quotas, bounded queues, maximum instances and a documented fallback/stop budget.

## Evaluation precision

Automate repeatable checks with fixed inputs and versioned expectations. Model judges, faithfulness scores and semantic reviews can be stochastic; record judge/configuration versions and disagreement rather than calling them deterministic truth.

## Module evidence to retain

module-engineering-evidence.json: dataset/release IDs; latency/cost/quality comparison; automated checks and critical failures; context and cache policy; deployment/failure observations. Mark unmeasured fields as not tested.

- Record latency, cost and quality for the boundary taught so far; mark unmeasured provider or deployment values unknown.
- Retain the taught positive and negative checks with unchanged expectations; keep semantic review separate.
- Explain the current source/context allowance and owner boundary; later cache or distributed controls are not assumed implemented.
- Exercise the failure path taught in this stage. Future hosting, overload and distributed recovery experiments become mandatory only in their own deployment stage.

exercise.solution:
## Complete guided-practice reference

Save the entire following block as solution.py and run `python3 -I solution.py` in a new scratch directory. No prior files or provider account are needed. This is one reference implementation of the bounded practice, not a completed live capstone.

```python
connections=240
safe_per_instance=12
minimum=(connections+safe_per_instance-1)//safe_per_instance
configured_max=10
assert minimum==20 and configured_max<minimum
print({'offered_connections':connections,'measured_safe_per_instance':12,
       'minimum_instances_at_capacity':minimum,'configured_max':configured_max,'admission_or_capacity_change_required':True})

# Guided practice reference implementation
def admit(offered,instances,safe_slots):
    if min(offered,instances,safe_slots)<0:raise ValueError('negative capacity')
    accepted=min(offered,instances*safe_slots)
    return {'offered':offered,'admitted':accepted,'rejected':offered-accepted}
assert admit(240,10,12)=={'offered':240,'admitted':120,'rejected':120}
assert admit(0,10,12)['rejected']==0
assert admit(10,0,12)['admitted']==0
print('practice:240 offered,120 admitted,120 rejected; zero replicas admit none')
```

## Expected reference observation

```text
{'offered_connections': 240, 'measured_safe_per_instance': 12, 'minimum_instances_at_capacity': 20, 'configured_max': 10, 'admission_or_capacity_change_required': True}
practice:240 offered,120 admitted,120 rejected; zero replicas admit none
```

## If your result differs

If the report says 240 users supported because offered=240, it confuses demand with capacity. The 12-slot figure is supplied fixture data; actual cloud measurements and reconnect tests are separate runbook tasks.

## Explain before continuing

Compare the changed code with the baseline: which new input or state transition is protected, and which integration behavior remains untested?

# Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets

## Before this session

Bring your notes and observed output from **Cloud Run/ECS concurrency and autoscaling**. Earlier completion clicks are not evidence of understanding: explain the input, output and failing case before adding this boundary.

### Specific preparation

## Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets · concepts and decision

## Before you begin

Session 32: capacity envelopes. GiB arithmetic below is illustrative and does not describe any particular model or GPU. Use Python3.12 with assertions enabled. All core practice runs offline with the standard library; provider accounts are only for separately labeled integration work.

## The case

A 24GiB illustrative budget leaves 5GiB after weights, runtime and safety headroom.

## Reason through the decision

Treat five 1GiB request slots as arithmetic only; actual hardware, batching, context and quality require measurement.

Self-hosting moves spend and operations to your GPU; it is not free inference. Resident weights, runtime buffers, safety headroom and KV cache all compete for memory. Context length and output length affect the per-request cache footprint. Ollama is a useful local-serving path; vLLM adds serving/batching controls for supported hardware/models. Quantization can change quality, so evaluate the exact artifact and tokenizer.

## Vocabulary used in this session

### Resident model memory

Weights/runtime allocations present before a user request.

### KV cache

Context-dependent attention state consuming inference memory.

### Artifact-specific evaluation

Quality and throughput measured for an exact model/quantization/runtime.

## Learn each concept step by step

Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Resident model memory

Resident memory includes weights and serving runtime before user context grows. Quantization changes the model artifact and memory footprint but can also change answer quality. Record model/license/revision, quantization, tokenizer, runtime and hardware so another operator can reproduce a comparison.

## Step 2 · KV cache

KV cache is attention state accumulated for input/output context during inference. More tokens and simultaneous requests generally require more memory, but the actual layout depends on model architecture, runtime, batching and cache management. Reserve runtime/headroom before estimating request slots; measured memory can differ from a worksheet.

## Step 3 · Artifact-specific evaluation

Artifact-specific evaluation compares the exact deployed model/runtime on identical labeled tasks. Ollama local streaming and a vLLM serving endpoint have different operational contracts even if a chat interface looks similar. Measure cold load, token lengths, throughput, p95, errors and quality. Fewer billed API calls do not make local GPU power/hardware/operations free.

## Read, run and explain the complete implementation

## Walk through the data and state

1. Subtract 14 weights,3 runtime and 2 headroom from 24 to leave 5 GiB.

2. At the supplied 1 GiB/request assumption that means five illustrative slots.

3. The result explicitly says real concurrency still requires measurement.

## Predict before execution

Save this entire block as example.py in an empty directory. Run `python3 -I example.py` with assertions enabled. It uses only the Python standard library, includes its synthetic data and performs no provider calls. Explain each assertion before running.

```python
# Illustrative GPU memory budget, not measurements of any model or device.
budget={'gpu_gib':24,'weights_gib':14,'runtime_gib':3,'safety_gib':2,'kv_per_request_gib':1}
remaining=budget['gpu_gib']-budget['weights_gib']-budget['runtime_gib']-budget['safety_gib']
slots=int(remaining//budget['kv_per_request_gib'])
assert slots==5
print({'illustrative_slots':slots,'real_concurrency_requires_measurement':True})
```

## Observed output

```text
{'illustrative_slots': 5, 'real_concurrency_requires_measurement': True}
```

## Transfer beyond the fixture

Self-hosting moves spend and operations to your GPU; it is not free inference. Resident weights, runtime buffers, safety headroom and KV cache all compete for memory. Context length and output length affect the per-request cache footprint. Ollama is a useful local-serving path; vLLM adds serving/batching controls for supported hardware/models. Quantization can change quality, so evaluate the exact artifact and tokenizer.

Run the documented local chat adapter against an installed model, then a GPU serving endpoint if hardware is available. Record model/license/revision, memory, cold-load time, tokens/sec, p95 and quality. Treat the five-slot fixture as arithmetic only; never use it as a device capacity claim.

## Complete integration: implementation and test boundaries

## Save and run the complete integration files

These files are part of this lesson, not a download assignment. Save each under the shown name in an isolated workspace. Use Python 3.12 and `python3 -m venv .venv`, then activate that environment. Only install packages for the integration you are running. Record resolved dependency versions with `python -m pip freeze > tested-dependencies.txt`; a version range is not a tested lock file. The standard-library experiment in the previous chapter needs none of these dependencies. Use synthetic data and your own authorized test accounts. Provider calls may incur charges; free academy enrollment does not include provider credits.

Install Ollama separately and explicitly select/download a model you are authorized to run; record its version/quantization and hardware. Install `httpx`, set `LOCAL_MODEL` and run `python provider_adapters.py` against the local Ollama endpoint. The adapter parses NDJSON deltas and requires a final done record before completion. import asyncio
```python
import json
import os

async def ollama_stream(messages,endpoint='http://127.0.0.1:11434',model=None):
    import httpx
    model=model or os.environ['LOCAL_MODEL']
    payload={'model':model,'messages':messages,'stream':True}

                               'output_tokens':item.get('eval_count'),'model':model}

async def cohere_rerank(query,candidates):
    import cohere
    if not query.strip() or not 1<=len(candidates)<=30:raise ValueError('query and 1–30 candidates required')
    client=cohere.AsyncClientV2(api_key=os.environ['COHERE_API_KEY'])
    async with asyncio.timeout(15):
        result=await client.rerank(model=os.environ['COHERE_RERANK_MODEL'],query=query,
                                  documents=[c['text'] for c in candidates],top_n=min(5,len(candidates)))
    ids=[]
    for row in result.results:
        if type(row.index) is not int or not 0<=row.index<len(candidates):raise ValueError('invalid rerank index')
        identifier=candidates[row.index]['id']
        if identifier in ids:raise ValueError('duplicate rerank result')
```

Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Resident model memory

Resident memory includes weights and serving runtime before user context grows. Quantization changes the model artifact and memory footprint but can also change answer quality. Record model/license/revision, quantization, tokenizer, runtime and hardware so another operator can reproduce a comparison.

## Step 2 · KV cache

KV cache is attention state accumulated for input/output context during inference. More tokens and simultaneous requests generally require more memory, but the actual layout depends on model architecture, runtime, batching and cache management. Reserve runtime/headroom before estimating request slots; measured memory can differ from a worksheet.

## Step 3 · Artifact-specific evaluation

Artifact-specific evaluation compares the exact deployed model/runtime on identical labeled tasks. ## Complete guided-practice reference

Save the entire following block as solution.py and run `python3 -I solution.py` in a new scratch directory. No prior files or provider account are needed. This is one reference implementation of the bounded practice, not a completed live capstone.

```python
# Illustrative GPU memory budget, not measurements of any model or device.
budget={'gpu_gib':24,'weights_gib':14,'runtime_gib':3,'safety_gib':2,'kv_per_request_gib':1}
remaining=budget['gpu_gib']-budget['weights_gib']-budget['runtime_gib']-budget['safety_gib']
slots=int(remaining//budget['kv_per_request_gib'])
assert slots==5
print({'illustrative_slots':slots,'real_concurrency_requires_measurement':True})

# Guided practice reference implementation
def estimated_slots(total,weights,runtime,safety,kv):
    if kv<=0 or min(total,weights,runtime,safety)<0:raise ValueError('invalid memory budget')
    remaining=total-weights-runtime-safety
    if remaining<0:raise ValueError('fixed allocations exceed device')
    return int(remaining//kv)
assert estimated_slots(24,14,3,2,1)==5
assert estimated_slots(24,14,3,2,2)==2
assert estimated_slots(19,14,3,2,1)==0
try:estimated_slots(18,14,3,2,1)
except ValueError:pass
else:raise AssertionError('overcommitted fixed memory accepted')
print('practice: doubling assumed KV reduces illustrative slots5→2; overcommit rejected')
```

# Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models

## Learning progression and project preparation

## Before this session

Bring your notes and observed output from **Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets**. Earlier completion clicks are not evidence of understanding: explain the input, output and failing case before adding this boundary.

### Specific preparation

- Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:33`)

If you cannot explain one of these mechanisms, return to that session’s trace and counterexample, rerun its reference, then retry your own version. The stable IDs identify lessons inside this program; no external enrollment is required.

## Readiness check from the previous session

Explain **Resident model memory** before continuing. Compare your explanation with this recap: Weights/runtime allocations present before a user request.

Reproduce the earlier positive case and its counterexample from your saved implementation. If you can only recall a passing output, reopen its walkthrough and explain why the counterexample must fail. Then identify what this session adds to that contract.

## Carry work forward

Keep one evidence folder for this stage: source input, implementation, unchanged expected labels, observed output and unresolved failures. Compare this lesson’s new boundary with the previous result. ## Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models · concepts and decision

## Before you begin

Sessions 3,22 and 32: concurrency, idempotency and cross-replica state. A token bucket permits a finite burst plus timed refill. Use Python3.12 with assertions enabled. All core practice runs offline with the standard library; provider accounts are only for separately labeled integration work.

## The case

Two replicas each enforce a local two-request bucket and jointly exceed the tenant limit.

## Reason through the decision

Use shared atomic enforcement and a clear overload response; evaluate fallback privacy, quality and spend separately.

Limit incoming requests separately from model-token budgets, worker concurrency and downstream provider quotas. A per-process bucket can be exceeded across replicas; a real distributed limiter needs atomic shared state and a chosen failure policy. Include Retry-After or a stable overload response and preserve accepted work. Fallback to another model/provider changes context capability, cost, privacy and quality, so it needs explicit routing and evaluation.

## Vocabulary used in this session

### Admission control

Rejecting work before exceeding a bounded resource budget.

### Atomic shared quota

Cross-replica accounting with defined failure/reconciliation behavior.

### Fallback contract

An evaluated alternative preserving authority, data and response constraints.

## Learn each concept step by step

Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Admission control

Admission control checks resources before expensive provider work. A request-rate bucket is distinct from simultaneous worker capacity, a token reservation and a monthly monetary budget. Two cheap short calls and two long generations can have the same request count but very different cost. Keep these limits explicit and report rejection.

## Step 2 · Atomic shared quota

An atomic shared quota means all workers update the same allowance as one indivisible operation. Separate local buckets each starting with two tokens can admit four aggregate requests. A durable conditional update or suitable shared-store primitive can enforce a global bound. Choosing shared state is not enough if check and decrement are separate races.

## Step 3 · Fallback contract

A fallback contract preserves authorization, permitted data location, output shape, deadline and evaluated quality. A failed quota store should follow an explicit fail-closed or bounded degraded policy; unlimited fallback can destroy the budget. Reserve estimated usage before work and reconcile actual usage afterward without double-refunding retried operation keys.

## Read, run and explain the complete implementation

## Walk through the data and state

1. Two requests at time 0 consume the initial burst of two tokens.

2. The third is rejected until refill supplies one token at time 1.

3. This baseline bucket is process-local, so it cannot establish a distributed bound.

## Predict before execution

Save this entire block as example.py in an empty directory. Run `python3 -I example.py` with assertions enabled. It uses only the Python standard library, includes its synthetic data and performs no provider calls. Explain each assertion before running.

```python
# Single-process token-bucket fixture. Replicas need a shared atomic store.
class Bucket:
    def __init__(self,capacity,refill):self.capacity=capacity;self.tokens=capacity;self.refill=refill;self.last=0
    def take(self,now,amount=1):
        self.tokens=min(self.capacity,self.tokens+(now-self.last)*self.refill);self.last=now
        if amount>self.tokens:return False
        self.tokens-=amount;return True
bucket=Bucket(2,1)
assert bucket.take(0) and bucket.take(0) and not bucket.take(0)
assert bucket.take(1)
print('burst bounded; one request admitted after refill; shared atomic store still required')
```

```text
burst bounded; one request admitted after refill; shared atomic store still required
```

Fallback to another model/provider changes context capability, cost, privacy and quality, so it needs explicit routing and evaluation.

## Apply the three engineering pillars

## Software-first practice

Build interfaces, asynchronous services, API adapters and recoverable data flows before studying algorithm derivations. Use mathematics to explain a measured engineering decision.

## Production evidence

A notebook or chat demo is an early prototype. Graduation builds toward operational evidence: deployment/readiness, bounded work, rate limits, error recovery and persisted state. Early checkpoints assess only boundaries already taught; future deployment controls are planned rather than claimed complete. The 10% framing is a teaching heuristic, not a measured universal percentage.

### Deterministic Evaluation

### Context Management

Budget resident model memory/KV cache and per-request context separately. Keep tenant/revision-aware application caches; never assume a process-local cache is shared across replicas.

## Complete guided-practice reference

Save the entire following block as solution.py and run `python3 -I solution.py` in a new scratch directory. No prior files or provider account are needed. This is one reference implementation of the bounded practice, not a completed live capstone.

```python
# Single-process token-bucket fixture. Replicas need a shared atomic store.
class Bucket:
    def __init__(self,capacity,refill):self.capacity=capacity;self.tokens=capacity;self.refill=refill;self.last=0
    def take(self,now,amount=1):

assert bucket.take(1)

# Guided practice reference implementation
import sqlite3,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path=Path(folder)/'quota.sqlite';first=sqlite3.connect(path);second=sqlite3.connect(path)
    first.execute('CREATE TABLE quota(owner TEXT PRIMARY KEY,remaining INTEGER)')
    with first:first.execute('INSERT INTO quota VALUES(?,?)',('acme',2))
    def reserve(db):
        with db:return db.execute('UPDATE quota SET remaining=remaining-1 WHERE owner=? AND remaining>=1',('acme',)).rowcount==1
    outcomes=[reserve(first),reserve(second),reserve(first),reserve(second)]
    assert outcomes==[True,True,False,False]
    assert first.execute('SELECT remaining FROM quota').fetchone()[0]==0
    first.close();second.close()
print('practice: two connections shared one atomic quota; two aggregate admissions, two rejections')
```

## Expected reference observation

```text
burst bounded; one request admitted after refill; shared atomic store still required
practice: two connections shared one atomic quota; two aggregate admissions, two rejections
```

If all four claims succeed, the connections are not sharing the same quota or the predicate is absent. Add operation-key reservation/refund and real multi-worker failure tests in the integration project; this exercise intentionally isolates atomic admission.

exercise.material:
## 1. Inspect the input and predict the outcome

1. Two requests at time 0 consume the initial burst of two tokens.

2. The third is rejected until refill supplies one token at time 1.

3. This baseline bucket is process-local, so it cannot establish a distributed bound.

```python
# Single-process token-bucket fixture. Replicas need a shared atomic store.
class Bucket:
    def __init__(self,capacity,refill):self.capacity=capacity;self.tokens=capacity;self.refill=refill;self.last=0
    def take(self,now,amount=1):
        self.tokens=min(self.capacity,self.tokens+(now-self.last)*self.refill);self.last=now
        if amount>self.tokens:return False
        self.tokens-=amount;return True
bucket=Bucket(2,1)
assert bucket.take(0) and bucket.take(0) and not bucket.take(0)
assert bucket.take(1)
print('burst bounded; one request admitted after refill; shared atomic store still required')
```

## Expected baseline observation

```text
burst bounded; one request admitted after refill; shared atomic store still required
```

## 2. Make the targeted change

Demonstrate shared atomic request reservations with two SQLite connections using one conditional UPDATE. Prove only two aggregate claims succeed.

# Hybrid-model SaaS integration and load experiments

## Learning progression and project preparation

## Before this session

Bring your notes and observed output from **Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models**. Earlier completion clicks are not evidence of understanding: explain the input, output and failing case before adding this boundary.

### Specific preparation

- Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:34`)

If you cannot explain one of these mechanisms, return to that session’s trace and counterexample, rerun its reference, then retry your own version. The stable IDs identify lessons inside this program; no external enrollment is required.

## Readiness check from the previous session

Explain **Admission control** before continuing. Compare your explanation with this recap: Rejecting work before exceeding a bounded resource budget.

Reproduce the earlier positive case and its counterexample from your saved implementation. If you can only recall a passing output, reopen its walkthrough and explain why the counterexample must fail. Then identify what this session adds to that contract.

## Carry work forward

Build toward **a deployed or explicitly local graduation packet**. Keep one evidence folder for this stage: source input, implementation, unchanged expected labels, observed output and unresolved failures. Compare this lesson’s new boundary with the previous result. The complete examples are independent fixtures: deliberately map their field names and source revisions before reusing code; do not concatenate scripts and assume their data agrees.

## Next checkpoint

Next: **Graduation release review and fresh-operator handover**. Save your current inputs, actual output and one unresolved question so the next session can extend a known baseline.

## Hybrid-model SaaS integration and load experiments · concepts and decision

## Before you begin

Sessions 29,33 and 34: accepted-output comparison, local model constraints and quotas. Use Python3.12 with assertions enabled. All core practice runs offline with the standard library; provider accounts are only for separately labeled integration work.

## The case

A locally approved private document triggers an automatic premium cloud fallback.

## Reason through the decision

Do not move the data silently; route only within consent/scope and compare hybrid with all-local/all-premium baselines.

Routing fixtures can verify a policy without proving that a classifier can recognize task difficulty. Evaluate route selection, output quality and escalation on the same cases. Hybrid serving needs consistent response contracts, context limits, trace correlation and tenant ownership across both endpoints. A premium fallback is not permission to move previously local confidential data off-device.

## Vocabulary used in this session

### Route selection

A measured decision about which model handles a particular task.

### Residency boundary

Where approved data may be processed, independent of model availability.

### Comparable workload

The same labeled inputs and conditions across candidate routes.

## Learn each concept step by step

Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Route selection

Route selection maps a request to an allowed execution path. The baseline uses supplied routine/complex labels, so it tests routing logic rather than a difficulty classifier. Unknown tasks go to review. To claim intelligent routing quality, independently label difficulty and compare route choices/output acceptance on held-out requests.

## Step 2 · Residency boundary

A residency boundary specifies where approved data may be processed. A premium cloud endpoint is not allowed for local-only material merely because a local model failed or ran out of context. Check data policy before selecting an adapter or cache, and keep the same owner/source revisions across paths.

## Step 3 · Comparable workload

Comparable workloads keep inputs, relevance labels, acceptance standards and measurement conditions fixed across all-local, all-premium and hybrid candidates. Include retries, fallback calls and review effort. A hybrid system can reduce one cost while raising tail latency or errors; a selected route is not itself a measured advantage.

## Read, run and explain the complete implementation

## Walk through the data and state

1. routine uses local, complex uses premium and unknown requires review.

2. A zero budget rejects even a routine request.

3. The baseline does not yet enforce data residency, exposing the extension needed next.

## Predict before execution

Save this entire block as example.py in an empty directory. Run `python3 -I example.py` with assertions enabled. It uses only the Python standard library, includes its synthetic data and performs no provider calls. Explain each assertion before running.

```python
requests=[{'id':'q1','kind':'routine','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q2','kind':'complex','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q3','kind':'unknown','owner':'acme'}]
def route(request,budget):
    if budget<=0:return 'budget_exhausted'
    if request['kind']=='routine':return 'local'
    if request['kind']=='complex':return 'premium'
    return 'review'
assert [route(r,10) for r in requests]==['local','premium','review']
assert route(requests[0],0)=='budget_exhausted'
print('routing contract checked; semantic difficulty classifier and quality remain unevaluated')
```

## Observed output

```text
routing contract checked; semantic difficulty classifier and quality remain unevaluated
```

## Transfer beyond the fixture

Routing fixtures can verify a policy without proving that a classifier can recognize task difficulty. Evaluate route selection, output quality and escalation on the same cases. Hybrid serving needs consistent response contracts, context limits, trace correlation and tenant ownership across both endpoints. A premium fallback is not permission to move previously local confidential data off-device.

Integrate the local/premium adapters with explicit data-routing consent, remaining-deadline checks and a capped budget. Compare all-premium, all-local and hybrid on a held-out workload. Test shared cache isolation, stale sources, provider failure and idempotent jobs across replicas.

## Connect the taught pieces before the capstone

# ai-engineering-12-week: complete independent student capstone

## Product and prerequisite contract

Ingest a synthetic source through /api/documents/ before asking about it. Trace owner filtering, fixed character chunks, ranking, a 700-character context cap and model routing. Compare routine_fixture with reasoning_fixture; both are transparent local adapters, not real local/frontier LLMs. Request review before the local effect.

Modules 1–3 teach adapter contracts, context/state, retrieval and reviewed actions; Module 4 teaches the release harness; sessions 31–35 teach containers, concurrency, routing and quotas. This is the reproducible local graduation route. Real voice/model/GPU/cloud experiments remain separately configured integrations, not a hidden dependency or a claimed test result.

The assembly mechanics below repair the previously missing connection between separate lesson examples. Read them before attempting the final project. Every file follows inline in the course; the optional program download contains the identical capstone/ directory. Python 3.12 and Docker Compose are required. There is no import from another academy program, Workshop checkout or private app database.

## Connect the pieces before changing them

1. Read core.py first. Its process(input, mode, documents) function returns a status, text and evidence IDs. It must never receive the expected test answer. The provider is a named scripted fixture, so a passing run proves control flow, not model quality.
2. Read app.py's exact and identity functions. Reject extra fields and blank input before retrieval. Demo bearer strings resolve to a trusted owner/role at the server; a JSON owner field is rejected. These published fixture tokens are local teaching identities, not production authentication.
3. Trace ask: validate → owner-filter persisted sources → core workflow → save result → return ID. A timeout is a stored failed result, not an empty successful answer. Health runs a real query against the required table.
4. initialize is a one-shot schema release job. It creates the records and quota tables before Gunicorn starts. PostgreSQL bucket is a fixed-minute quota window: avoid the reserved SQL word window. Parameterized values stay outside SQL syntax. The ON CONFLICT increment is atomic across both HTTP workers; a Python dictionary counter would not be shared.
5. PostgreSQL JSONB stores an object, but Django raw cursors may return its JSON text. Decode a string at the storage boundary before accessing fields. Do not serialize an already serialized value twice. All reads include owner before payload leaves the database.
6. Approval digests bind text, source version and citations using one canonical server serialization. The UI uses the server's digest rather than trying to recreate Python JSON spacing in JavaScript. The submitted version and digest must match the row locked by SELECT FOR UPDATE. Only reviewer-one can approve owner one's draft. The effect is a local outbox row, never an external message, refund or calendar event.
7. The same transaction writes the local effect and approval status. A stable effect key plus the row lock makes simultaneous duplicate confirmation return the same receipt. A timed-out external write would need reconciliation; this local transaction does not claim distributed exactly-once delivery.
8. Browser code displays response text with textContent and retains the input on errors. It shows the stored result before review. An HTTP 201 says a result was saved; inspect status to distinguish needs_review, failed, abstain, denied or needs_correction.
9. Compose starts an isolated PostgreSQL volume, runs the schema job once, and publishes only the API on loopback. Recreating an API container must retain records because the database volume is separate. Dependency outage yields 503; health is not a substitute for the full check script.
10. check.py sends real HTTP requests and reads back their actual IDs. It tests changed approvals, wrong owners, malformed input, failures and concurrent duplicate review. Latency is measured around actual requests. Unknown token usage and spend remain null, not fabricated zero. This sequential local sample is not a cloud concurrency benchmark.

## Make the three pillars observable

Compare two core candidates on the same unchanged cases; retain failed and rejected work in the report. Measure HTTP latency separately from any future provider latency and report accepted-output quality. Preserve exact deterministic invariants while recording factual review separately. Context budgets here are explicitly characters; token accounting belongs in an actual model adapter. Scope and source revisions belong in any future cache key; no cache-hit or savings claim is made by these local projects.

## Diagnose a failed build or check

If schema exits nonzero, inspect that service's log before testing the API. If HTTP succeeds but the saved result differs, inspect core.process and the stored JSON separately. If a restart loses data, inspect the named volume and compose project name. If a duplicate approval changes receipts, inspect the row-lock/transaction boundary, not the prompt. Preserve the failed output with its repaired rerun.

<!-- student-depth:start -->
## Student build walkthrough — a bounded local SaaS release, with honest upgrade boundaries

The earlier voice, mixed-media, workspace and evaluation integration files remain separate runnable projects. This graduation service combines a narrower path: persisted synthetic text → scoped lexical retrieval → one of two scripted routes → reviewable draft → local receipt. The two routes do not call real local or frontier models. Cloud autoscaling, speech quality and GPU throughput need the separately taught deployment/provider experiments; this local service cannot certify them.

### Step 1 — carry the actual taught retrieval invariant into the build

Session 8 now contains the exact `select_context` function used by core.py. Run its published tests first:

```sh
python3.12 -m unittest -v test_core
```

The paragraph fixture deliberately places “Opened items are excluded” after character 350. The old fixed-character split could return the rule while dropping that exclusion. The current implementation keeps reviewed paragraph units intact, retains source ID/position/revision, and refuses a relevant unit that exceeds its 700-character allowance. needs_correction is visible and contains no answer or citations. It is safer than silently slicing an exclusion out of evidence.

The allowance counts evidence characters before join separators, not provider tokens. Owner filtering is the SQL adapter’s job before it calls the pure function. An irrelevant oversized paragraph is excluded by ranking; a relevant oversized paragraph requires a reviewed split. This is a deliberate conservative policy, not an optimal semantic chunker.

### Step 2 — follow storage identity and context through one request

`documents` derives an ID from owner and the exact text digest. Same owner/same bytes return the same identity; another owner cannot reuse that ID to read private content. This local fixture keeps every uploaded document searchable. It does not choose active policy versions or resolve contradictory uploads. Keep one approved policy per source for this scoped release; the ingestion/index-migration lessons teach the explicit activation mechanism needed before expanding that claim.

`ask` fetches only the authenticated owner’s documents, then `select_context` ranks whole units. The route selects routine_fixture or reasoning_fixture from the declared query rule. Both extract source text. The candidate cache key uses canonical JSON containing pipeline version, selected route, query and evidence revisions; it is an identity for a future cache, not an implemented hit or measured savings. Source IDs contain owner in this service. A general cache must also bind trusted owner/permission state explicitly and invalidate on revocation.

### Step 3 — interpret the evaluation denominator correctly

Run check.py, then evaluate.py in a fresh quota window as documented. Its 120 HTTP observations cover ten families with twelve variants each. Labels stay in the harness. A timeout or 429 remains a failed observation, not a row to delete. Four clients measure this bounded local workload; they do not simulate thousands of concurrent users or independent semantic tasks.

Session 29’s runtime studio now calculates cost per accepted result from all attempted work and leaves partial cost unknown. In this capstone, cost_usd and provider token usage remain null because no model is called. A passed mechanical release harness is not a measured faithfulness score. Retain a separate source-support review for any future real adapter and record model/prompt/dataset versions and disagreement.

### Step 4 — use failure evidence to decide the next change

| Failure | Repair at the taught boundary | Do not substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exception lost from context | Reviewed evidence-unit boundary in session 8 | A valid citation ID alone |
| Another owner sees source text | Owner predicate before retrieval | Post-generation redaction |
| Oversized relevant unit | Review its split or change a measured budget | Silent truncation |
| Identical candidate key after source change | Canonical source revision identity | Calling an unimplemented cache a hit |
| Partial cost reported as complete | Unknown-cost counter and undefined ratio | Zero for unavailable billing |

Student extension: before modifying the retriever, add a policy whose exclusion occurs after the old cut and prove the complete exclusion survives HTTP readback. Then add a relevant oversized unit and require needs_correction. Keep this test corpus separate from evaluate.py’s frozen corpus: injecting an intentionally oversized relevant policy changes the candidate environment. Use a dedicated fresh Compose project/volume for the extension, then run restart, outage and restoration drills on its exact IDs. Do not delete another project’s data to get a clean score.

### Read a failed acceptance report

The HTTP check starts a fresh report before its first request and updates it as checks run. A failed assertion or dependency exception leaves completed=false, the checks observed so far and error_type; it still exits nonzero. A completed=true report means the whole procedure finished. Latency p95 uses nearest rank, ceil(.95*n)-1, over its labeled sample. Do not reuse an older successful report after a new failed run, and do not mistake twelve sequential observations for a capacity benchmark.
<!-- student-depth:end -->



The final project chapter in this program provides every file, exact commands and the failure checks. Explain the storage, ownership and observed-result boundaries above before proceeding. No code from another program is required.

## Practice first, then integrate

## Your practical task

1. Read the concept tutorial, trace the complete baseline and predict its assertions before running.

2. Add local-only residency and remaining-deadline gates before route selection. Verify no premium route is returned for restricted data.

3. Run your change against the named normal and failure cases. Compare actual output with the reference only after making your own attempt.

Integrate the local/premium adapters with explicit data-routing consent, remaining-deadline checks and a capped budget. Compare all-premium, all-local and hybrid on a held-out workload. Test shared cache isolation, stale sources, provider failure and idempotent jobs across replicas.

Complete the bounded task first. Carry its invariant and tests into this larger project. Earlier sessions and the inline integration files supply the building blocks; optional live providers must be tested separately. A successful local reference is not evidence of cloud scale, speech quality or real connector effects.

## Review before marking complete

The exercise includes staged hints, a full reference solution and diagnostic feedback. Compare after your own attempt. Practical submission is your own evidence report, not automated code inspection or certification.

## Apply the three engineering pillars

## Software-first practice

Build interfaces, asynchronous services, API adapters and recoverable data flows before studying algorithm derivations. Use mathematics to explain a measured engineering decision.

## Production evidence

A notebook or chat demo is an early prototype. Graduation builds toward operational evidence: deployment/readiness, bounded work, rate limits, error recovery and persisted state. Early checkpoints assess only boundaries already taught; future deployment controls are planned rather than claimed complete. The 10% framing is a teaching heuristic, not a measured universal percentage.

## Module evidence to retain

chapters.body:
## Before you begin

Sessions 29,33 and 34: accepted-output comparison, local model constraints and quotas. Use Python3.12 with assertions enabled. All core practice runs offline with the standard library; provider accounts are only for separately labeled integration work.

## The case

A locally approved private document triggers an automatic premium cloud fallback.

## Reason through the decision

Do not move the data silently; route only within consent/scope and compare hybrid with all-local/all-premium baselines.

Routing fixtures can verify a policy without proving that a classifier can recognize task difficulty. Evaluate route selection, output quality and escalation on the same cases. Hybrid serving needs consistent response contracts, context limits, trace correlation and tenant ownership across both endpoints. A premium fallback is not permission to move previously local confidential data off-device.

## Vocabulary used in this session

### Route selection

A measured decision about which model handles a particular task.

### Residency boundary

Where approved data may be processed, independent of model availability.

### Comparable workload

The same labeled inputs and conditions across candidate routes.

chapters.title: Learn each concept step by step
chapters.body:
Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Route selection

Route selection maps a request to an allowed execution path. The baseline uses supplied routine/complex labels, so it tests routing logic rather than a difficulty classifier. Unknown tasks go to review. To claim intelligent routing quality, independently label difficulty and compare route choices/output acceptance on held-out requests.

## Step 2 · Residency boundary

A residency boundary specifies where approved data may be processed. A premium cloud endpoint is not allowed for local-only material merely because a local model failed or ran out of context. Check data policy before selecting an adapter or cache, and keep the same owner/source revisions across paths.

## Step 3 · Comparable workload

Comparable workloads keep inputs, relevance labels, acceptance standards and measurement conditions fixed across all-local, all-premium and hybrid candidates. Include retries, fallback calls and review effort. A hybrid system can reduce one cost while raising tail latency or errors; a selected route is not itself a measured advantage.

1. routine uses local, complex uses premium and unknown requires review.

2. A zero budget rejects even a routine request.

3. The baseline does not yet enforce data residency, exposing the extension needed next.

## Predict before execution

Save this entire block as example.py in an empty directory. Run `python3 -I example.py` with assertions enabled. It uses only the Python standard library, includes its synthetic data and performs no provider calls. Explain each assertion before running.

```python
requests=[{'id':'q1','kind':'routine','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q2','kind':'complex','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q3','kind':'unknown','owner':'acme'}]
def route(request,budget):
    if budget<=0:return 'budget_exhausted'
    if request['kind']=='routine':return 'local'
    if request['kind']=='complex':return 'premium'
    return 'review'
assert [route(r,10) for r in requests]==['local','premium','review']
assert route(requests[0],0)=='budget_exhausted'
print('routing contract checked; semantic difficulty classifier and quality remain unevaluated')
```


## Transfer beyond the fixture

Routing fixtures can verify a policy without proving that a classifier can recognize task difficulty. Evaluate route selection, output quality and escalation on the same cases. Hybrid serving needs consistent response contracts, context limits, trace correlation and tenant ownership across both endpoints. A premium fallback is not permission to move previously local confidential data off-device.

chapters.title: Connect the taught pieces before the capstone
chapters.body:
# ai-engineering-12-week: complete independent student capstone

## Product and prerequisite contract

Ingest a synthetic source through /api/documents/ before asking about it. Trace owner filtering, fixed character chunks, ranking, a 700-character context cap and model routing. Compare routine_fixture with reasoning_fixture; both are transparent local adapters, not real local/frontier LLMs. Request review before the local effect.

Modules 1–3 teach adapter contracts, context/state, retrieval and reviewed actions; Module 4 teaches the release harness; sessions 31–35 teach containers, concurrency, routing and quotas. This is the reproducible local graduation route. Real voice/model/GPU/cloud experiments remain separately configured integrations, not a hidden dependency or a claimed test result.

The assembly mechanics below repair the previously missing connection between separate lesson examples. Read them before attempting the final project. Every file follows inline in the course; the optional program download contains the identical capstone/ directory. Python 3.12 and Docker Compose are required. There is no import from another academy program, Workshop checkout or private app database.

## Connect the pieces before changing them

1. Read core.py first. Its process(input, mode, documents) function returns a status, text and evidence IDs. It must never receive the expected test answer. The provider is a named scripted fixture, so a passing run proves control flow, not model quality.
2. Read app.py's exact and identity functions. Reject extra fields and blank input before retrieval. Demo bearer strings resolve to a trusted owner/role at the server; a JSON owner field is rejected. These published fixture tokens are local teaching identities, not production authentication.
3. Trace ask: validate → owner-filter persisted sources → core workflow → save result → return ID. A timeout is a stored failed result, not an empty successful answer. Health runs a real query against the required table.
4. initialize is a one-shot schema release job. It creates the records and quota tables before Gunicorn starts. PostgreSQL bucket is a fixed-minute quota window: avoid the reserved SQL word window. Parameterized values stay outside SQL syntax. The ON CONFLICT increment is atomic across both HTTP workers; a Python dictionary counter would not be shared.
5. PostgreSQL JSONB stores an object, but Django raw cursors may return its JSON text. Decode a string at the storage boundary before accessing fields. Do not serialize an already serialized value twice. All reads include owner before payload leaves the database.
6. Approval digests bind text, source version and citations using one canonical server serialization. The UI uses the server's digest rather than trying to recreate Python JSON spacing in JavaScript. The submitted version and digest must match the row locked by SELECT FOR UPDATE. Only reviewer-one can approve owner one's draft. The effect is a local outbox row, never an external message, refund or calendar event.
7. The same transaction writes the local effect and approval status. A stable effect key plus the row lock makes simultaneous duplicate confirmation return the same receipt. A timed-out external write would need reconciliation; this local transaction does not claim distributed exactly-once delivery.
8. Browser code displays response text with textContent and retains the input on errors. It shows the stored result before review. An HTTP 201 says a result was saved; inspect status to distinguish needs_review, failed, abstain, denied or needs_correction.
9. Compose starts an isolated PostgreSQL volume, runs the schema job once, and publishes only the API on loopback. Recreating an API container must retain records because the database volume is separate. Dependency outage yields 503; health is not a substitute for the full check script.
10. check.py sends real HTTP requests and reads back their actual IDs. It tests changed approvals, wrong owners, malformed input, failures and concurrent duplicate review. Latency is measured around actual requests. Unknown token usage and spend remain null, not fabricated zero. This sequential local sample is not a cloud concurrency benchmark.

## Make the three pillars observable

Compare two core candidates on the same unchanged cases; retain failed and rejected work in the report. Measure HTTP latency separately from any future provider latency and report accepted-output quality. Preserve exact deterministic invariants while recording factual review separately. Context budgets here are explicitly characters; token accounting belongs in an actual model adapter. Scope and source revisions belong in any future cache key; no cache-hit or savings claim is made by these local projects.

## Diagnose a failed build or check

If schema exits nonzero, inspect that service's log before testing the API. If HTTP succeeds but the saved result differs, inspect core.process and the stored JSON separately. If a restart loses data, inspect the named volume and compose project name. If a duplicate approval changes receipts, inspect the row-lock/transaction boundary, not the prompt. Preserve the failed output with its repaired rerun.

<!-- student-depth:start -->
## Student build walkthrough — a bounded local SaaS release, with honest upgrade boundaries

The earlier voice, mixed-media, workspace and evaluation integration files remain separate runnable projects. This graduation service combines a narrower path: persisted synthetic text → scoped lexical retrieval → one of two scripted routes → reviewable draft → local receipt. The two routes do not call real local or frontier models. Cloud autoscaling, speech quality and GPU throughput need the separately taught deployment/provider experiments; this local service cannot certify them.

### Step 1 — carry the actual taught retrieval invariant into the build

Session 8 now contains the exact `select_context` function used by core.py. Run its published tests first:

```sh
python3.12 -m unittest -v test_core
```

The paragraph fixture deliberately places “Opened items are excluded” after character 350. The old fixed-character split could return the rule while dropping that exclusion. The current implementation keeps reviewed paragraph units intact, retains source ID/position/revision, and refuses a relevant unit that exceeds its 700-character allowance. needs_correction is visible and contains no answer or citations. It is safer than silently slicing an exclusion out of evidence.

The allowance counts evidence characters before join separators, not provider tokens. Owner filtering is the SQL adapter’s job before it calls the pure function. An irrelevant oversized paragraph is excluded by ranking; a relevant oversized paragraph requires a reviewed split. This is a deliberate conservative policy, not an optimal semantic chunker.

### Step 2 — follow storage identity and context through one request

`documents` derives an ID from owner and the exact text digest. Same owner/same bytes return the same identity; another owner cannot reuse that ID to read private content. This local fixture keeps every uploaded document searchable. It does not choose active policy versions or resolve contradictory uploads. Keep one approved policy per source for this scoped release; the ingestion/index-migration lessons teach the explicit activation mechanism needed before expanding that claim.

`ask` fetches only the authenticated owner’s documents, then `select_context` ranks whole units. The route selects routine_fixture or reasoning_fixture from the declared query rule. Both extract source text. The candidate cache key uses canonical JSON containing pipeline version, selected route, query and evidence revisions; it is an identity for a future cache, not an implemented hit or measured savings. Source IDs contain owner in this service. A general cache must also bind trusted owner/permission state explicitly and invalidate on revocation.

### Step 3 — interpret the evaluation denominator correctly

Run check.py, then evaluate.py in a fresh quota window as documented. Its 120 HTTP observations cover ten families with twelve variants each. Labels stay in the harness. A timeout or 429 remains a failed observation, not a row to delete. Four clients measure this bounded local workload; they do not simulate thousands of concurrent users or independent semantic tasks.

Session 29’s runtime studio now calculates cost per accepted result from all attempted work and leaves partial cost unknown. In this capstone, cost_usd and provider token usage remain null because no model is called. A passed mechanical release harness is not a measured faithfulness score. Retain a separate source-support review for any future real adapter and record model/prompt/dataset versions and disagreement.

### Step 4 — use failure evidence to decide the next change

| Failure | Repair at the taught boundary | Do not substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exception lost from context | Reviewed evidence-unit boundary in session 8 | A valid citation ID alone |
| Another owner sees source text | Owner predicate before retrieval | Post-generation redaction |
| Oversized relevant unit | Review its split or change a measured budget | Silent truncation |
| Identical candidate key after source change | Canonical source revision identity | Calling an unimplemented cache a hit |
| Partial cost reported as complete | Unknown-cost counter and undefined ratio | Zero for unavailable billing |

Student extension: before modifying the retriever, add a policy whose exclusion occurs after the old cut and prove the complete exclusion survives HTTP readback. Then add a relevant oversized unit and require needs_correction. Keep this test corpus separate from evaluate.py’s frozen corpus: injecting an intentionally oversized relevant policy changes the candidate environment. Use a dedicated fresh Compose project/volume for the extension, then run restart, outage and restoration drills on its exact IDs. Do not delete another project’s data to get a clean score.

### Read a failed acceptance report

The HTTP check starts a fresh report before its first request and updates it as checks run. A failed assertion or dependency exception leaves completed=false, the checks observed so far and error_type; it still exits nonzero. A completed=true report means the whole procedure finished. Latency p95 uses nearest rank, ceil(.95*n)-1, over its labeled sample. Do not reuse an older successful report after a new failed run, and do not mistake twelve sequential observations for a capacity benchmark.
<!-- student-depth:end -->



The final project chapter in this program provides every file, exact commands and the failure checks. Explain the storage, ownership and observed-result boundaries above before proceeding. No code from another program is required.

chapters.title: Apply the three engineering pillars
chapters.body:
## Software-first practice

Build interfaces, asynchronous services, API adapters and recoverable data flows before studying algorithm derivations. Use mathematics to explain a measured engineering decision.

## Production evidence

A notebook or chat demo is an early prototype. Graduation builds toward operational evidence: deployment/readiness, bounded work, rate limits, error recovery and persisted state. Early checkpoints assess only boundaries already taught; future deployment controls are planned rather than claimed complete. The 10% framing is a teaching heuristic, not a measured universal percentage.

## Apply the three pillars to A multi-user AI service deployed from containers

### Latency vs. Cost vs. Quality

Load-test offered vs. completed work, p95 and cost per accepted result at stated concurrency. Autoscaling settings are hypotheses until observed against downstream/GPU limits.

### Deterministic Evaluation

Test readiness against the actual database, restart/readback, isolated restore, denied owner access, overload rejection and a dependency outage on the deployed revision.

### Context Management

Budget resident model memory/KV cache and per-request context separately. Keep tenant/revision-aware application caches; never assume a process-local cache is shared across replicas.

## Failure and deployment work

Separate request concurrency, worker capacity and model/GPU capacity. Add admission control, shared quotas, bounded queues, maximum instances and a documented fallback/stop budget.

## Evaluation precision

Automate repeatable checks with fixed inputs and versioned expectations. Model judges, faithfulness scores and semantic reviews can be stochastic; record judge/configuration versions and disagreement rather than calling them deterministic truth.

## Module evidence to retain

module-engineering-evidence.json: dataset/release IDs; latency/cost/quality comparison; automated checks and critical failures; context and cache policy; deployment/failure observations. Mark unmeasured fields as not tested.

- Record latency, cost and quality for the boundary taught so far; mark unmeasured provider or deployment values unknown.
- Retain the taught positive and negative checks with unchanged expectations; keep semantic review separate.
- Explain the current source/context allowance and owner boundary; later cache or distributed controls are not assumed implemented.
- Exercise the failure path taught in this stage. Future hosting, overload and distributed recovery experiments become mandatory only in their own deployment stage.

## Complete guided-practice reference

Save the entire following block as solution.py and run `python3 -I solution.py` in a new scratch directory. No prior files or provider account are needed. This is one reference implementation of the bounded practice, not a completed live capstone.

```python
requests=[{'id':'q1','kind':'routine','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q2','kind':'complex','owner':'acme'}, {'id':'q3','kind':'unknown','owner':'acme'}]
def route(request,budget):
    if budget<=0:return 'budget_exhausted'
    if request['kind']=='routine':return 'local'
    if request['kind']=='complex':return 'premium'
    return 'review'
assert [route(r,10) for r in requests]==['local','premium','review']
assert route(requests[0],0)=='budget_exhausted'
print('routing contract checked; semantic difficulty classifier and quality remain unevaluated')

# Guided practice reference implementation
def safe_route(request,budget,remaining_ms,cloud_allowed):
    if budget<=0:return 'budget_exhausted'
    if remaining_ms<=0:return 'deadline_exhausted'
    if request['kind']=='complex' and not cloud_allowed:return 'review'
    return route(request,budget)
complex_request={'kind':'complex','owner':'acme'}
assert safe_route(complex_request,10,100,False)=='review'
assert safe_route(complex_request,10,100,True)=='premium'
assert safe_route(complex_request,10,0,True)=='deadline_exhausted'
assert safe_route(complex_request,0,100,True)=='budget_exhausted'
print('practice: residency/deadline/budget checked before premium routing')
```

## Expected reference observation

```text
routing contract checked; semantic difficulty classifier and quality remain unevaluated
practice: residency/deadline/budget checked before premium routing
```

## If your result differs

If restricted input reaches premium, fallback has expanded data access. If an expired deadline still calls a model, admission is too late. The capstone must measure actual route quality and cost rather than use these fixture labels as a classifier.

## Explain before continuing

Compare the changed code with the baseline: which new input or state transition is protected, and which integration behavior remains untested?

lessons.content:
# Graduation release review and fresh-operator handover

## Learning progression and project preparation

## Before this session

Bring your notes and observed output from **Hybrid-model SaaS integration and load experiments**. Earlier completion clicks are not evidence of understanding: explain the input, output and failing case before adding this boundary.

### Specific preparation

- Workspace agent capstone (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:24`)
- LLMOps stress-test capstone (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:30`)
- Containers, network boundaries and persistent state (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:31`)
- Cloud Run/ECS concurrency and autoscaling (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:32`)
- Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:33`)
- Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:34`)
- Hybrid-model SaaS integration and load experiments (`academy-v2:ai-engineering-12-week:35`)

If you cannot explain one of these mechanisms, return to that session’s trace and counterexample, rerun its reference, then retry your own version. The stable IDs identify lessons inside this program; no external enrollment is required.

## Readiness check from the previous session

Explain **Route selection** before continuing. Compare your explanation with this recap: A measured decision about which model handles a particular task.

Reproduce the earlier positive case and its counterexample from your saved implementation. If you can only recall a passing output, reopen its walkthrough and explain why the counterexample must fail. Then identify what this session adds to that contract.

## Carry work forward

Build toward **a deployed or explicitly local graduation packet**. Keep one evidence folder for this stage: source input, implementation, unchanged expected labels, observed output and unresolved failures. Compare this lesson’s new boundary with the previous result. The complete examples are independent fixtures: deliberately map their field names and source revisions before reusing code; do not concatenate scripts and assume their data agrees.

## Taught-to-project evidence map

- **prior integrated agent and release evidence** — taught in Workspace agent capstone, LLMOps stress-test capstone. Evidence: retain those lessons’ successful case and negative check in the project report.
- **containers and concurrency** — taught in Containers, network boundaries and persistent state, Cloud Run/ECS concurrency and autoscaling. Evidence: retain those lessons’ successful case and negative check in the project report.
- **local-model capacity and distributed budgets** — taught in Ollama, vLLM and GPU memory/context budgets, Distributed quotas, budgets and fallback models. Evidence: retain those lessons’ successful case and negative check in the project report.
- **hybrid routing and load experiment** — taught in Hybrid-model SaaS integration and load experiments. Evidence: retain those lessons’ successful case and negative check in the project report.

## Assemble, then test

Reuse the candidate and regression cases, then add the taught hybrid routing, quota and load experiment. Rehearse fresh-operator setup and recovery. Each release field is passed, failed or untested; only observed passed checks may support a release claim. A local run is an honest local graduation path; cloud scale requires the actual deployment/load evidence, not configuration alone.

## Feedback when integration fails

Find the first boundary whose actual output differs from its contract. Rerun that lesson’s isolated positive and negative checks. If they pass, inspect the connecting field names, owner/source IDs, units and state transitions; do not weaken the gold labels or bypass a denied path. Record the failing input and unresolved result. Passing a single variation does not establish the whole project.

## Completion boundary

Reopen the evidence packet in a fresh session. A complete program records both successful checks and remaining limits. Choose further study by the missing capability; another academy program is optional, not a hidden graduation prerequisite.

## Graduation release review and fresh-operator handover · concepts and decision

## Before you begin

The final release assembles the five module projects. Use their actual evidence; the local practice below only validates a release-packet checker. Use Python3.12 with assertions enabled. All core practice runs offline with the standard library; provider accounts are only for separately labeled integration work.

## The case

Every checkbox except the real load report is green; the README claims thousands of concurrent users.

## Reason through the decision

Withhold the scale claim, complete the missing observation or narrow the release statement and handover scope.

Graduation is an evidence-backed release decision, not an automatic production-ready label. The final SaaS must connect tenant authentication, source-grounded work, reviewed actions, hybrid models, persistent state, evaluation, observability, quotas and recovery. Autoscaling configuration alone does not establish thousands of concurrent users. Unknown or unmet gates remain visible and constrain the claim.

## Vocabulary used in this session

### Release evidence

Observed quality, capacity, recovery and ownership for the candidate.

### Unmet gate

A missing or failing requirement that remains visible at decision time.

### Scoped readiness claim

A capability claim limited to tested workload and operational conditions.

## Learn each concept step by step

Read these three explanations before running the specimen. Each connects a definition to the decision it controls.

## Step 1 · Release evidence

Release evidence is an inspectable observation tied to the candidate: dataset/manifest IDs, accepted quality, all-attempt spend, latency population, load envelope, owner-isolation results, restart/restore and operational ownership. A checkbox is a claim; the packet needs underlying reports and a reproducible procedure.

## Step 2 · Unmet gate

An unmet gate can be failed or untested. Represent missing evidence explicitly and refuse to turn a nonempty string like “not tested” into True. Critical gates cannot be overridden by an attractive average or a deployment badge. Give each blocker an owner, reason and next observation; do not label an unknown result as passed.

```python
 out.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2));print(json.dumps({'passed':len(observations),'program':kind,'report':str(out)}))
```

```python
"""Local hybrid-routing SaaS: two transparent adapters, actual persisted sources."""
import re,hashlib,json
KIND='engineering'
VERSION='engineering-router-v2'
def select_context(text,documents,budget=700):
 """Owner filtering is the caller's responsibility, before passing documents."""
 terms=set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+',text.lower()))
 ranked=[]
 for document in documents:
  # A blank-line-delimited evidence unit must retain its rule and exceptions.
  # Oversized relevant units require a reviewed split, never silent truncation.
  for position,unit in enumerate(document['text'].split('\n\n')):
   unit=unit.strip()
   score=len(terms & set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+',unit.lower())))
   if score:ranked.append((score,document['id']+':'+str(position),unit,document['revision']))
 ranked.sort(key=lambda row:(-row[0],row[1]));selected=[];used=0
 if any(len(row[2])>budget for row in ranked):
  raise ValueError('relevant evidence unit needs a reviewed split')
 for score,id,chunk,revision in ranked:
  if used+len(chunk)<=budget:selected.append((id,chunk,revision));used+=len(chunk)
 return selected,used

def process(text,mode,documents):
 terms=set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+',text.lower()))
 if terms & {'send','delete','schedule'}:return {'status':'denied','text':None,'citations':[],'trace':['permission_gate']}
 if mode=='timeout':raise TimeoutError('fixture')
 if mode=='malformed':raise ValueError('fixture')
 # The tokenizer is an explicit word baseline, not measured model tokens.
 try:selected,used=select_context(text,documents)
 except ValueError:
  return {'status':'needs_correction','text':None,'citations':[],
          'issues':['relevant_evidence_unit_exceeds_700_characters'],
          'trace':['owner_filter','paragraph_units','rank','reviewed_split_required']}
 if not selected:return {'status':'abstain','text':None,'citations':[],'context_chars':0,'trace':['owner_filter','paragraph_units','rank','no_evidence']}
 model='reasoning_fixture' if terms & {'compare','exceptions','conflict'} else 'routine_fixture'
 # Both use a source-extractive fixture so the complete path is reproducible.
 answer=' '.join(row[1] for row in selected)
 cache_inputs={'model':model,'pipeline':VERSION,'query':text,
               'evidence':[(row[0],row[2]) for row in selected]}
 cache_key=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(cache_inputs,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest()
 return {'status':'needs_review','text':answer,'citations':[r[0] for r in selected], 'model':model,'context_chars':used,'cache_key':cache_key,'cache_hit':False,'trace':['owner_filter','paragraph_units','rank','context_budget','route_'+model,'validated_draft','await_review']}
```
